PetroSA PART 2

By: Joy Summers | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
He has bought and sold a soccer club, he owns multimillion rand homes in the best suburbs, and until recently he owned a Bentley Continental as part of his fleet of luxury cars. Meet Shumani Lawrence

Unique Selling Point:
Big national story where we have all the evidence. Colourful and controversial main character and a very clear case of secret flawed deals being kept from the public.

Summary:
Now Lawrence Mulaudzi is set to become South Africa’s new gas oligarch- thanks to state owned company PetroSA who have chosen his company Equator Holdings, as the preferred supplier to both fund and rehabilitate a multimillion rand overhaul of their gas infrastructure outside of Mossel Bay and even parts of the Gas to Liquid plant.

So is Mulaudzi really the best man for the job? He is neither a solid financial institution or an expert in gas reconstruction. Instead he is tainted by allegations of corruption for his wheeling and dealing at the PIC, where he raked in over R40 million rand in success fees. In 2023 he had to give back his Bentley that was about to be repossessed, and when he didn’t pay his office rent a property company were about to auction off his multimillion rand mansion in Bantry Bay. He also had to sell his soccer club.

So it’s difficult to understand Petrosa’s rational and defence of Mulaudzi as a preferred supplier in a process that is clearly flawed. According to the French publication Africa intelligence, the choice of Mulaudzi may have something to do with the ties he has to Gwede Mantashe’s wife. But PetroSA are standing firm, and their decision seems to have got the green light from Audit firm Mazars. Has State capture 2.0 moved from Megawatt Park to Mossel Bay.


Further information:
The hooks we will hang the story on are as follows:

• South Africa’s resources are once again for sale to the politically connected, and the deals are being signed in secret, at Petrosa.

• Petrosa, a controversial business man Lawrence Mulaudzi, and the political elite, aided and abetted by Mazars, an audit and accounting advisory, are going down the same dodgy road taken previously by Transnet and Eskom.

• Billions were spent on uncovering the state capture project and the failure of Eskom and Transnet continue to be a massive drain on the country’s resources. President Ramaphosa came into office on the ticket to clean up corruption, and yet here we are again.

• Who is Lawrence Mulaudzi and why is it a bad idea to turn him into South Africa’s new gas baron. Out of 60 million south Africans why choose him?

• Even PetroSA’s deal with the Russian company Gazprom bank will not be as significant as this deal with Mulaudzi and his directors of Equator Holdings, who stand to benefit from a profit sharing arrangement over thousands of kilometers of offshore gas fields that should benefit the country, and not a handful of private individuals.

• Why is no- one stopping the deal that is fraught with conflict of interest, violations of governance, proper tender processes and sound reasoning?

• In the light of grey listing and all the commitments of president Cyril Ramaphosa, this deal that PetroSA has defended in writing, makes no sense unless it is viewed through a cynical lens – that Mulaudzi has been selected as a money funnel, a role that he has embarked on before at the PIC.

PETROSA PART 2 FINAL SCRIPT FOR TX SUNDAY 26th FEB


Voice over 1
It’s bigger than the Kruger National Park. 23 200 km2 of oil and gas exploration rights off our Southern Cape Coast.
This is block 9/ 11A of South Africa’s undersea oil and gas riches.

Up sound

PetroSA, the state- owned oil and gas company is on an aggressive drive to extract the maximum amount of oil and gas from this field, and they have already chosen their private partners in multibillion rand deals shrouded in secrecy.

Partners that will later share in the profits.

Beat pause
This is the story of one of those deals - RFP 0004/2023
Fade to black

Voice over 2
In December we broadcast our first investigation into PetroSA, and how this state owned company had burned through billions till it was bankrupt, and survived only because Minerals and Energy Minister Gwede Mantashe’s department insisted Eskom buy diesel from the parastatal.

Gwede Mantashe
Now if you want to expose the business of PetroSA you are basically killing it

Voice over 3
When questioned, the minister justified the lack of transparency around the diesel sales and PetroSA refused to be interviewed. But then the day after our broadcast, they called a Press conference.
Sandisiwe Ncemane former Acting CEO: PetroSA
It's unfortunate that the relentless leaking of company information to the media persists

Susan Comrie
They have this press conference, which they never do. They're incredibly secretive, most of the time.

VO 4
A recent R3.5 billion rand deal with Russian company Gazprom Bank, exposed by investigative journalist Susan Comrie and covered by Carte Blanche, had made them angry.

Brief up Sound Susan walking with Masa

But the deal with Gazprom, to revive a refinery in Mossel Bay, shocked even gas industry insiders. Apart from a sanctions risk the tender process appeared flawed. But the Gazprom deal was only the beginning.

Susan
What we discovered is that later that same day, they go and hold a private signing ceremony to finalise an even bigger deal.

VO 5
The deal- RFP 0004 would make the company, Equator Holdings, a major player in the offshore gas industry. The face of Equator is director Lawrence Mulaudzi - a politically exposed businessman with a controversial past.

Susan Comrie
I was shocked, to be honest, when I found out who they were proposing to bring in, Lawrence Mulaudzi. I just sort of said, surely not him?! You know, it was like a jaw dropping moment.

MASA LINK
So who is this man that PetroSA have placed front and centre of their massive new gas transaction?

Dr. Lumkile Mondi
The unique thing about Mulaudzi is that he is the chosen one.

VO 6
Dr Lumkile Mondi is an economist and lecturer at Wits Business School. He has worked with high level international organisations whose aim is to prevent a repeat of the state capture project.

Masa Kekana
You know, this deal with Equator Holdings is quite significant. It's double the annual budget of the Department of Energy and yet it seems to be only benefiting a handful of people and not the country itself.

Dr Lumkile Mondi
That's the nature of oligarchy. Oligarchy is a scheme where business interests and politicians interests intersect, in their interaction is to keep those two in power. So from a business perspective, to keep me knowing I'm the only guy in town- from a political perspective, is to keep me in power for forever

VO 7
A closer look at this Limpopo multimillionaire, reveals 68 pages of companies and directorships, A sprawling R12,5 million rand incomplete mansion, in one of the country’s richest neighbourhoods.

Music up sound.
Another R19 million rand home on Cape Town’s Atlantic Seaboard.
Two years ago he bought a premier league soccer club for a reported R35 million, but sold it 8 months later amidst reports that the players were not being paid. Beautiful cars completed the picture, including a Bentley Continental.

A new one will set you back around R5 to R6 million rand

Masa
Is Mr. Lawrence Mulaudzi South Africa's new gas baron?
Dr. Lumkile Mondi
Absolutely! But he's one of a few who are part of a broader economy. So in oligarchy there are those individuals who are the chosen.

VO 8
And yet ironically when Equator bid against Gazprom to restore the Mossel Bay refinery, it wasn’t chosen. The tenders ran almost concurrently but Equator was eliminated from that one, scoring a zero in that bid.

SUSAN COMRIE
You literally score him zero because you say you can't establish even basic facts about the company. Yet on the other tender you say, fantastic, let's go with this guy. This is our man!

VO 9
When Equator was first selected for RFP 0004, it was only a funding deal. PetroSA needs about R22 billion rand for the exploration and development of their gas wells. But the deal ballooned, and now Equator will be contracted to finance and reinstate the gas infrastructure. Compared to the Gazprom deal, this one is enormous.

Susan
When you plot it out on a map and you look at the portion that Gazprom is doing versus all of the different projects that Equator is now going to do, you realise that they've really walked away with a kind of lion's share of this deal.

VO10
The RFP 0004 tender required an established player or a credible financial institution. If not, according to their own documents, the bid would be eliminated. Equator was neither.

SUSAN COMRIE
They've been around for a number of years, but they have almost no presence. you can't find a website. It's very difficult to even find any information about who works there. You know, the company address, for instance, seems to be Mr. Mulaudzi home in Sandhurst

VO11
In this letter to Carte Blanche, Mulaudzi lists this home as the address of Equator holdings, but when we checked it out, earlier this month, it looked more like an abandoned construction site than the headquarters of a credible financial institution.

Music up sound

But this wasn't the end of the red flag road.

MASA LINK TO CAMERA
If a state owned company entrusted you to raise over R20 billion rand to restart South Africa’s offshore gas industry, it would probably be a good idea to ensure you have an impeccable financial record right? But Lawrence Mulaudzi has had a string of bad debts and almost had his CT mansion auctioned just to pay off one of them.




VO 12
A last minute payment saved the Cape Mansion from going under the hammer, but he was unable to keep the Bentley and it was reportedly sold on auction in 2022.

Masa
I mean, he couldn't keep up the instalment of his swanky Bentley?
Susan Comrie
You know, he's having to go out there as Equator, going to banks, to these large financial institutions and saying, trust me, with R22 billion worth of your money. They're going to be looking at how banks have had to go to court to try and force him to pay his debts. And it's going to be very unlikely that they're going to be willing to give him a cent.

LINK
Lawrence Mulaudzi says he can't do an interview with us because he is away, but in his letter he defends the deal and says, and I quote “We have every intention to deliver and we will!” He further states:

‘The project will benefit the country.. and that Equator Holdings complied with PetroSA requirements and there were no grounds to disqualify it.’

VO 13
But even if PetroSA overlooked his bad debts, why are they ignoring his past? Mulaudzi is tainted by deals made with the Public Investment Corporation - a fund that largely looks after government pension money.

Up sound Mulaudzi
When he made that request to me ….



VO 14
In 2019 he testified at the Mpati commission of Inquiry into Corruption at the PIC, about deals he’d made with its top officials.

SUSAN COMRIE
When you look at all of the transactions that he's been involved in along the way, you see various politically connected people, politicians sort of circling around Mr. Mulaudzi, many of them who seemingly seem to have their hands out looking for money from him and he's more than willing, it seems, to sort of dish out that money where it's needed

VO 15
In his letter to Carte Blanche, Mulaudzi says that throughout the process he was transparent, truthful and forthright with the commission.

MASA
But did the Mpati commission actually clear him?
SUSAN COMRIE
I would say absolutely not.

VO 16
But PetroSA signed with Equator anyway. It also has an additional 6 months to come up with the money even though that was the point of the tender. Equator will also do a feasibility study, to see if the project is actually viable.

All this- just as Minister Mantashe pushes gas as the new emerging fuel to keep the lights on, a bounty for rent seekers.

Dr. Lumkile Mondi
So what about a much more emerging sector which has got far higher rents than these others and can be able to swing the law without transparency, and using national interest as a shield, as we've seen in the past under apartheid regime, and now we're seeing it also coming back to haunt us, in the name, today of a just energy transition.

VO 17
But even if Equator’s deal fails, Mulaudzi has a back up plan. A 10 % slice of a partnership called Equatheza. This company will develop the gas reserves in this 22 000 square kilometre gas field PetroSA called block 9/11 A

Exactly how he was given the 10% is not clear. Did PetroSA arrange a marriage? No, says Mulaudzi, the new joint venture was formed independently and voluntarily without the assistance of PetroSA.

Susan Comrie
It feels like going back to the initial days of state capture when tenders were being crudely manipulated.

V0 18
And perhaps we should listen when the evidence leader at the Zondo Commission of Enquiry into State Capture, Paul Pretorius, warns that the country may be facing a new period of state capture.

Paul Pretorius
The whole purpose of a commission of inquiry is not to have another one in five years’ time and say what the hell happened?

LINK
So it's fair to ask, what was PetroSA thinking? In deals like this in a post Zondo era, governance matters, and the board will have to defend their decisions, but can they defend this one?


VO 19
But it’s the shareholder the board must answer to, and in this case -it’s minerals and energy Minister, Gwede Mantashe. Does he not see the red flags that we do?

Dr. Lumkile Mondi
When you connect the dots you'll see that this money is all going to move very quickly, be paid very quickly before even the work is done.

Paul Pretorius
I like to think that corruption now is simply a virus in a different variant, needing new approaches and needing new forms of combating. Unfortunately, we don't see that happening

VO 20
Once again PetroSA would not do an interview, instead they sent us a broad press statement, in which they commit to respect the governance processes and conduct the necessary due diligence on these new gas deals. Or our interpretation - nothing to see here, move along.


THE END

PROMO ONE
Link
Recently PetroSA have signed a multibillion rand gas deal with a controversial businessman, but if you are looking for accountability, they’re not saying much
Susan
They have this press conference which they never do, they are incredibly secretive, what we discover is that later that same day, they go and hold a private signing ceremony to finalise an even bigger deal

PROMO TWO Lumkile
When you connect the dots you will see that this money is going to move very quickly before even the work is done, we have seen this game before.

VOICE OVER
PetroSA needs around R22 billion to fix its dilapidated gas infrastructure, and they have recently signed a massive profit sharing deal, but who are their business partners?

PROMO THREE
PetroSA is on an aggressive drive to revitalise our oil and gas industry, but will the recent deals its signed benefit South Africa or just a few chosen elites.

Lumkile Mondi
That is the nature of Oligarchy, oligarchy is a scheme where business interests and politician interests intersect to keep those two in power.





























OUT TAKE COMM

VO 18
questionable deals being rushed through before elections? Why aren’t the future profits going straight to treasury to create sovereign wealth for the country?

Susan Comrie You know, he's having to go out there as Equator, going to banks, to these large financial institutions and saying, trust me, with R22 billion worth of your money. They're going to be looking at how banks have had to go to court to try and force him to pay his debts. And it's going to be very unlikely that they're going to be willing to give him a cent. LINK Lawrence Mulaudzi says he can't do an interview with us because he is away, but in his letter he defends the deal and says, and I quote “We have every intention to deliver and we will!” He further states: ‘The project will benefit the country.. and that Equator Holdings complied with PetroSA requirements and there were no grounds to disqualify it.’ VO 13 But even if PetroSA overlooked his bad debts, why are they ignoring his past? Mulaudzi is tainted by deals made with the Public Investment Corporation - a fund that largely looks after government pension money. Up sound Mulaudzi When he made that request to me …. VO 14 In 2019 he testified at the Mpati commission of Inquiry into Corruption at the PIC, about deals he’d made with its top officials. SUSAN COMRIE When you look at all of the transactions that he's been involved in along the way, you see various politically connected people, politicians sort of circling around Mr. Mulaudzi, many of them who seemingly seem to have their hands out looking for money from him and he's more than willing, it seems, to sort of dish out that money where it's needed VO 15 In his letter to Carte Blanche, Mulaudzi says that throughout the process he was transparent, truthful and forthright with the commission. MASA But did the Mpati commission actually clear him? SUSAN COMRIE I would say absolutely not. VO 16 But PetroSA signed with Equator anyway. It also has an additional 6 months to come up with the money even though that was the point of the tender. Equator will also do a feasibility study, to see if the project is actually viable. All this- just as Minister Mantashe pushes gas as the new emerging fuel to keep the lights on, a bounty for rent seekers. Dr. Lumkile Mondi So what about a much more emerging sector which has got far higher rents than these others and can be able to swing the law without transparency, and using national interest as a shield, as we've seen in the past under apartheid regime, and now we're seeing it also coming back to haunt us, in the name, today of a just energy transition. VO 17 But even if Equator’s deal fails, Mulaudzi has a back up plan. A 10 % slice of a partnership called Equatheza. This company will develop the gas reserves in this 22 000 square kilometre gas field PetroSA called block 9/11 A Exactly how he was given the 10% is not clear. Did PetroSA arrange a marriage? No, says Mulaudzi, the new joint venture was formed independently and voluntarily without the assistance of PetroSA. Susan Comrie It feels like going back to the initial days of state capture when tenders were being crudely manipulated. V0 18 And perhaps we should listen when the evidence leader at the Zondo Commission of Enquiry into State Capture, Paul Pretorius, warns that the country may be facing a new period of state capture. Paul Pretorius The whole purpose of a commission of inquiry is not to have another one in five years’ time and say what the hell happened? LINK So it's fair to ask, what was PetroSA thinking? In deals like this in a post Zondo era, governance matters, and the board will have to defend their decisions, but can they defend this one? VO 19 But it’s the shareholder the board must answer to, and in this case -it’s minerals and energy Minister, Gwede Mantashe. Does he not see the red flags that we do? Dr. Lumkile Mondi When you connect the dots you'll see that this money is all going to move very quickly, be paid very quickly before even the work is done. Paul Pretorius I like to think that corruption now is simply a virus in a different variant, needing new approaches and needing new forms of combating. Unfortunately, we don't see that happening VO 20 Once again PetroSA would not do an interview, instead they sent us a broad press statement, in which they commit to respect the governance processes and conduct the necessary due diligence on these new gas deals. Or our interpretation - nothing to see here, move along. THE END PROMO ONE Link Recently PetroSA have signed a multibillion rand gas deal with a controversial businessman, but if you are looking for accountability, they’re not saying much Susan They have this press conference which they never do, they are incredibly secretive, what we discover is that later that same day, they go and hold a private signing ceremony to finalise an even bigger deal PROMO TWO Lumkile When you connect the dots you will see that this money is going to move very quickly before even the work is done, we have seen this game before. VOICE OVER PetroSA needs around R22 billion to fix its dilapidated gas infrastructure, and they have recently signed a massive profit sharing deal, but who are their business partners? PROMO THREE PetroSA is on an aggressive drive to revitalise our oil and gas industry, but will the recent deals its signed benefit South Africa or just a few chosen elites. Lumkile Mondi That is the nature of Oligarchy, oligarchy is a scheme where business interests and politician interests intersect to keep those two in power. OUT TAKE COMM VO 18 questionable deals being rushed through before elections? Why aren’t the future profits going straight to treasury to create sovereign wealth for the country? PAGE 1.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): He has bought and sold a soccer club, he owns multimillion rand homes in the best suburbs, and until recently he owned a Bentley Continental as part of his fleet of luxury cars. Meet Shumani Lawrence
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Big national story where we have all the evidence. Colourful and controversial main character and a very clear case of secret flawed deals being kept from the public.
metadata.Summary: Now Lawrence Mulaudzi is set to become South Africa’s new gas oligarch- thanks to state owned company PetroSA who have chosen his company Equator Holdings, as the preferred supplier to both fund and rehabilitate a multimillion rand overhaul of their gas infrastructure outside of Mossel Bay and even parts of the Gas to Liquid plant. So is Mulaudzi really the best man for the job? He is neither a solid financial institution or an expert in gas reconstruction. Instead he is tainted by allegations of corruption for his wheeling and dealing at the PIC, where he raked in over R40 million rand in success fees. In 2023 he had to give back his Bentley that was about to be repossessed, and when he didn’t pay his office rent a property company were about to auction off his multimillion rand mansion in Bantry Bay. He also had to sell his soccer club. So it’s difficult to understand Petrosa’s rational and defence of Mulaudzi as a preferred supplier in a process that is clearly flawed. According to the French publication Africa intelligence, the choice of Mulaudzi may have something to do with the ties he has to Gwede Mantashe’s wife. But PetroSA are standing firm, and their decision seems to have got the green light from Audit firm Mazars. Has State capture 2.0 moved from Megawatt Park to Mossel Bay.
metadata.Further information: The hooks we will hang the story on are as follows: • South Africa’s resources are once again for sale to the politically connected, and the deals are being signed in secret, at Petrosa. • Petrosa, a controversial business man Lawrence Mulaudzi, and the political elite, aided and abetted by Mazars, an audit and accounting advisory, are going down the same dodgy road taken previously by Transnet and Eskom. • Billions were spent on uncovering the state capture project and the failure of Eskom and Transnet continue to be a massive drain on the country’s resources. President Ramaphosa came into office on the ticket to clean up corruption, and yet here we are again. • Who is Lawrence Mulaudzi and why is it a bad idea to turn him into South Africa’s new gas baron. Out of 60 million south Africans why choose him? • Even PetroSA’s deal with the Russian company Gazprom bank will not be as significant as this deal with Mulaudzi and his directors of Equator Holdings, who stand to benefit from a profit sharing arrangement over thousands of kilometers of offshore gas fields that should benefit the country, and not a handful of private individuals. • Why is no- one stopping the deal that is fraught with conflict of interest, violations of governance, proper tender processes and sound reasoning? • In the light of grey listing and all the commitments of president Cyril Ramaphosa, this deal that PetroSA has defended in writing, makes no sense unless it is viewed through a cynical lens – that Mulaudzi has been selected as a money funnel, a role that he has embarked on before at the PIC.
